questions.stem: A client who can become pregnant is starting isotretinoin and says, “I am not sexually active, so the pregnancy-prevention program does not apply to me.” Which response is most accurate in August 2026?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"You are exempt from iPLEDGE because FDA ended the isotretinoin pregnancy-safety program when it approved program changes in February 2026.","B":"Isotretinoin remains under iPLEDGE for embryo-fetal risk; current program safeguards still apply, including FDA-authorized pregnancy-testing flexibilities.","C":"Only a pregnancy test after the final dose is required because FDA eliminated pretreatment pregnancy testing for every patient starting isotretinoin in 2026.","D":"iPLEDGE applies only to patients who report current sexual activity; documented abstinence automatically removes pregnancy-testing and program requirements."}}
questions.rationale: As of August 14, 2026, iPLEDGE remains in effect to mitigate embryo-fetal risk. FDA delayed implementation of the approved 2026 modifications to November 15, 2026, and until implementation is complete FDA continues its stated enforcement discretion for certain pregnancy-testing requirements. The absence of current sexual activity does not mean the iPLEDGE program itself no longer applies.
questions.source_name: FDA — iPLEDGE Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS)
questions.source_detail: FDA iPLEDGE REMS page, June 16, 2026 update: implementation of approved modifications delayed to November 15, 2026; until full implementation FDA continues stated enforcement discretion regarding certain pregnancy-testing requirements. Reviewed 2026-08-14.

questions.stem: A client with a T4 spinal cord injury suddenly develops a pounding headache, facial flushing, profuse sweating above the lesion, and blood pressure 210/120 mm Hg. Which nursing action is the priority?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Place the client flat and elevate the legs because the primary problem is loss of vascular tone with severe hypotension from the high spinal cord injury.","B":"Administer routine analgesia and reassess in one hour because headache and sweating are expected chronic manifestations after an injury above T6.","C":"Encourage the client to bear down and increase abdominal pressure because autonomic dysreflexia is usually relieved by increasing stimulation below the lesion.","D":"Sit the client upright, rapidly assess for triggers such as bladder or bowel distention, monitor blood pressure closely, and escalate emergency management."}}
questions.rationale: The presentation is classic for autonomic dysreflexia, a potentially life-threatening hypertensive emergency in people with spinal cord injury, commonly at or above T6. The PVA Consortium guideline directs immediate upright positioning, frequent blood-pressure and pulse monitoring, and prompt identification and removal of provoking stimuli, beginning with urinary causes.
questions.source_name: Paralyzed Veterans of America / Consortium for Spinal Cord Medicine — Evaluation and Management of Autonomic Dysreflexia and Other Autonomic Dysfunctions
questions.source_detail: Current PVA Consortium CPG listing reviewed 2026-08-14; direct published guideline: Krassioukov et al., Top Spinal Cord Inj Rehabil. 2021;27(2):225-290, DOI 10.46292/sci2702-225, Recommendations 2.1 and 2.5-2.13. Acute management includes immediately sitting the individual upright, frequent BP/pulse monitoring, and urinary-trigger evaluation.

questions.stem: A client with asthma has a written action plan based on peak expiratory flow. Which statement shows correct understanding of home peak-flow monitoring?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"I will compare each reading with a population-predicted value because my own best measurement should not be used to guide an individualized action plan.","B":"I will compare readings with my established personal best and follow the written action-plan zones and instructions when values fall from that baseline.","C":"I need to measure peak flow only during a severe attack because routine or symptom-triggered trends cannot provide useful information about worsening control.","D":"If my peak flow falls, I will ignore symptoms and use the number alone because action plans should not incorporate clinical changes or medication instructions."}}
questions.rationale: CDC asthma action-plan guidance uses individualized green, yellow, and red zones and expresses peak expiratory flow relative to the person's best peak flow. The client should compare readings with the established personal best and follow the written action-plan instructions rather than rely on a population value or an isolated number.
questions.source_name: CDC — Living with Asthma: Asthma Action Plan
questions.source_detail: CDC Living with Asthma page, Asthma Action Plan Green/Yellow/Red Zone section: peak flow zones are expressed as percentages of the individual's best peak flow. Page dated May 4, 2026; reviewed 2026-08-14.

questions.stem: A postmenopausal client with low bone mass asks which lifestyle plan best supports bone health while the provider completes a fracture-risk assessment. Which response is best?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Avoid weight-bearing activity because repetitive loading accelerates bone loss once bone mineral density has already begun to decline.","B":"Use adequate calcium and vitamin D intake with appropriate weight-bearing and muscle-strengthening activity tailored to fracture risk.","C":"Increase caffeine intake and avoid resistance exercise because stimulants and rest provide the strongest protection against fragility fractures.","D":"Rely on vitamin supplements alone because exercise, balance training, and fall-risk reduction do not materially affect fracture prevention."}}
questions.rationale: BHOF prevention guidance supports adequate calcium and vitamin D together with weight-bearing and muscle-strengthening exercise. Exercise selection should reflect fracture risk and physical limitations rather than applying a one-size-fits-all high-impact program.
questions.source_detail: BHOF Prevention page, Calcium and Vitamin D plus Exercise for Strong Bones sections: adequate calcium/vitamin D and both weight-bearing and muscle-strengthening exercise are part of bone-health prevention. Reviewed 2026-08-14.

questions.stem: An asymptomatic, average-risk 47-year-old adult asks whether colorectal cancer screening can wait until age 50. Which response best reflects the current USPSTF recommendation?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Screening should begin now because the USPSTF recommends colorectal cancer screening for average-risk adults ages 45 to 49 as a Grade B service.","B":"Screening should wait until age 50 because the USPSTF gives no recommendation for asymptomatic average-risk adults before age 50 unless symptoms appear.","C":"Screening is recommended only after age 75 because earlier testing has no net benefit for asymptomatic adults who do not have a family history.","D":"Screening should begin before age 50 only when a first-degree relative had colorectal cancer, because age alone does not support screening at 47."}}
questions.rationale: The USPSTF final recommendation dated May 18, 2021 gives a Grade B recommendation to screen average-risk adults ages 45 to 49 for colorectal cancer and Grade A for ages 50 to 75. It applies to asymptomatic adults at average risk. As of August 14, 2026, colorectal cancer screening is not listed among USPSTF recommendations in progress, so the 2021 final recommendation remains the current published USPSTF statement.
questions.source_name: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force — Colorectal Cancer: Screening
questions.source_detail: USPSTF Final Recommendation Statement, May 18, 2021, Recommendation Summary and Patient Population Under Consideration: adults ages 45-49, Grade B; asymptomatic adults at average risk. Currentness checked against USPSTF Recommendations in Progress on 2026-08-14.
